AC1.note: src/trigger/config.ts validates .metaproject/triggers.json per entry; a malformed entry is refused on load with its reason and the rest still load (src/trigger/config.test.ts), duplicate names rejected

AC2.note: keryx trigger run <name> does one pass; exit non-zero only when the action failed, nothing-to-do exits 0 with a no-op outcome (src/commands/trigger-run.e2e.test.ts)

AC5.note: keryx trigger install extends the managed hook block via src/lib/managed-hook.ts; post-merge and post-checkout sync behaviour survives, pre-existing hooks kept (src/commands/trigger-hooks-coexist.test.ts)

AC6.note: keryx trigger schedule prints a cron line or a systemd unit with absolute paths and no daemon; the printed line is executed as the scheduler would run it, and the unit passes systemd-analyze verify (src/commands/trigger-schedule.e2e.test.ts, src/trigger/schedule.test.ts)

AC7.note: skipIfOpen checks for an equivalent open flow inside the run lock; the second firing is a no-op with a stated reason (src/commands/trigger-run-open-flow.e2e.test.ts)

AC8.note: evaluateTriggerBudget refuses before spending, outcome budget-refused in the ledger; an unreadable ledger fails closed, not open (src/trigger/run.test.ts)

AC9.note: README triggers section and docs CLI reference cover the config, the commands and that scheduling is the operator scheduler's job
